rv.q: It's a magnetic performance well-suited to Max Hunter's staging, which opts for exclamation points over question marks and successfully brings the play into 2026.
The Pass is an unsentimental look at what one must give up in order to obtain fame and fortune in professional sports—a bet plenty are still willing to take.
"The Pass" is something of a tease — sexy, twisty, suspenseful, but also downbeat and misleading.
Under Max Hunter's sluggish and scattered direction, the actors struggle to maintain our interest over a two-hour, intermissionless running time.

cn.t: Critics find this US debut of Donnelly's 2014 soccer drama a dark, realistic look at closeted athletes and toxic masculinity, though reactions are mixed on its execution and relevance twelve years later.
